issues.description: Install scripts now hardcode python3.12 instead of finding the best available python
issues.detail: The Amazon/Rocky prep steps were changed from installing a discoverable python (previously python39 on Rocky) to forcing python3.12 specifically. The rest of the matrix still tests 3.10, 3.11, 3.12. Pin the minimum (3.10) or read the matrix version, otherwise CI silently tests only one interpreter on those distros while claiming broader coverage. Data and intent are out of sync.

issues.description: Three UP rules disabled wholesale with a TODO defers the actual cleanup
issues.detail: UP045/UP007/UP035 are exactly the rules that would enforce the new A | None style this PR advertises. Disabling them with a TODO means the codebase keeps both shapes indefinitely. Either land the sweep now or scope the ignore to specific paths so new code is held to the new shape. A blanket repo-wide ignore is the wrong data structure for a migration.

issues.description: default_raise and accompanying comments still reference dead <3.10 compatibility
issues.detail: default_raise is documented as existing for <3.10 compatibility, and a comment block above TransactionEndpointRequest still says "this is for < 3.10 compatibility". With 3.9 gone, decide whether default_raise earns its keep on its own merits, and remove the stale rationale. Right now the data (code) and the documentation (comments) disagree.

issues.description: Debug-flavored dnf search left in production install matrix
issues.detail: The new Amazon/Rocky prep steps run `dnf search python3.12` between update and install. Search output is noise in CI logs and serves no functional purpose; if discovery matters, do it once locally and drop the line. Small, but it's the kind of cleverness that lingers because nobody owns it.

issues.description: itertools.pairwise swap is a nice 3.10 win worth applying more broadly
issues.detail: Replacing zip(ordered, ordered[1:]) with itertools.pairwise is exactly the kind of data-shape simplification this version bump unlocks. Grep the rest of the tree for the same zip-with-tail pattern and apply uniformly while the migration is fresh; otherwise the codebase carries two idioms for the same thing.

review.summary: A clean removal of a version branch — the diff is mostly subtraction, which is the right shape for this kind of work. The structural concerns are: install-script prep now pins 3.12 directly instead of letting the matrix drive the version, and three lint rules that would enforce the new type-union style are disabled repo-wide with a TODO, deferring the real cleanup. A few stale <3.10 comments and a missed itertools.pairwise opportunity round out the nits. Data dominates: the codebase should pick one shape (PEP 604 unions, no version branches) and let the tooling enforce it, rather than leaving both shapes coexisting.
